overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: no quorum met on June 30, 2010, so no notice was required, and no lawful emergency existed because the COLA deadline was foreseeable.

allegations.summary: A board member allegedly interfered with posting notice for a June 30, 2010 emergency meeting, which the complainant said should have been allowed to proceed.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that Board member Bean did not violate the Open Meeting Law by preventing notice from being posted for this meeting, since no meeting was held on that date requiring notice.

allegations.summary: The complainant contended an emergency existed because the Board learned on June 29, 2010 it had to vote by June 30 on the COLA, so the 48-hour notice rule could be set aside.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, we find that it would have been improper for the Board to hold an emergency meeting on June 30, 2010.
